version.changelog: Bundled Node.js scripts replace raw curl — eliminates shell injection surface. Auth, call, and status operations run through auditable .mjs files. Privacy section added.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions broadly match a phone-calling service, but there are a few mismatches and choices (a staging/default gateway URL, a different homepage domain, and the ability to point the gateway via env var) that warrant caution before installing or trusting it with sensitive data.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description and bundled scripts clearly implement a phone-calling/negotiation capability and require only node — that is coherent. However, the SKILL.md/homepage point to 'pineclaw.com' while the scripts interact with '19pine.ai' (and a staging gateway host) which is a domain mismatch that is unexpected and should be verified with the vendor.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions confine actions to the Pine service: authenticate via email/code, start calls, poll status, and save tokens locally. The SKILL.md explicitly instructs collecting potentially sensitive 'callee_context' (authentication/payment info) from users — this is functionally required for many calls but increases privacy risk and should be limited to what is strictly necessary.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no external install step (no archive download or package install). The skill ships small Node scripts and runs them with the node binary; nothing in the install mechanism writes outside its own credential path or creates system-wide artifacts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no unrelated credentials and stores its own Pine access token under ~/.pine-voice/credentials.json (written with 0600 permissions). However, the scripts default to a 'staging' gateway URL (agent3-api-gateway-staging.19pine.ai) and allow overriding the gateway via PINE_GATEWAY_URL. This means network endpoints can be redirected (intentionally or accidentally), which could route call audio/metadata to an unexpected host. Also, SKILL.md asks the user to provide their Pine account email and verification code — appropriate for authentication but a potential social-engineering surface if the agent asks for other credentials.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always: true' and only persists its own credentials file under the user's home directory. It does not modify other skills or system-wide configs; autonomous invocation is allowed but that is the platform default.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement the advertised calling capability, but check these before you install/use it: 1) Verify the vendor: the SKILL.md/homepage differs from the API domain used by the scripts (pineclaw.com vs 19pine.ai) — confirm these belong to the same service. 2) Confirm the gateway: the scripts default to a staging gateway (agent3-api-gateway-staging.19pine.ai) and allow overriding PINE_GATEWAY_URL — ask the vendor whether production endpoints should be used and avoid running with an untrusted gateway. 3) Protect sensitive inputs: the skill asks you to supply call context (may include auth or payment info). Do not provide full card numbers, SSNs, passwords, or other secrets unless absolutely necessary. 4) Credential storage: tokens are saved at ~/.pine-voice/credentials.json with 0600 perms — you can inspect or remove this file if needed. 5) Billing and privacy: confirm who processes and stores transcripts and whether calls incur charges. 6) If you have doubts, contact the vendor to confirm domains and endpoints or avoid providing real customer credentials — consider using a limited/test Pine account for risk-limited trials.
